diagnostic_evidence.quote: For all \(\mathbf{x}_* \in \overline{\left\{\mathbf{x} : \mathbf{x} + \int_{t^*}^{t_2} \mathbf{A}(\mathbf{s}(\tau), \tau) \, \mathrm{d}\tau \in \operatorname{supp}\{\Psi\}\right\}}\), \quad we have \(\mathbf{x}_* + \int_{t^*}^{t_2} \mathbf{A}(\mathbf{s}(\tau), \tau) \, \mathrm{d}\tau \in \operatorname{supp}\{\Psi\}\). \quad This implies \(\Psi\left(\mathbf{x}_* + \int_{t^*}^{t_2} \mathbf{A}(\mathbf{s}(\tau), \tau) \, \mathrm{d}\tau\right) \neq 0\)

issues.failure_explanation: The proof treats supp{ψ} as {ψ ≠ 0} and supp{Ψ} as {Ψ ≠ 0}. Under the standard definition (support = closure of the nonzero set), points of the support may have ψ = 0 or Ψ = 0. The first bullet asserts ψ(x*,t*) ≠ 0 for x* in the support, which fails at boundary points of the nonzero set. The second bullet asserts that membership of a mapped point in supp{Ψ} implies Ψ ≠ 0 at that point, which likewise fails at the boundary. Both implications are invalid as written. The lemma's statement (supp{ψ(x,t*)} = CODE_{t2→t*}(Ω)) is correct and can be established using the fact that the flow map is a diffeomorphism and that preimages of closed sets under continuous maps are closed, but the written proof does not do this.

failure_location.quote: For all \(\mathbf{x}^* \in \operatorname{supp}\{\psi(\mathbf{x}, t^*)\}\), where \(t^* \in [t_1, t_2]\), we have \(\psi(\mathbf{x}^*, t^*) \neq 0\).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rewrite the proof to use the standard definition of support (closure of the nonzero set) and invoke the diffeomorphism property of the flow map to show that the preimage of the closed set supp{Ψ} under the flow is closed and equals CODE_{t2→t*}(Ω).
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Lemma lemma-psi-supp is invalid as written, but the lemma's statement is correct and no downstream result depends on the faulty proof steps (the existence proof uses only the weaker consequence supp{ψ^0} ⊂ Ω̃^{1,0}, which holds regardless).
issues.title: Support lemma proof equates support with nonzero set and mishandles closures
issues.why_classification: The lemma's statement is correct and all downstream uses are unaffected. A short local proof rewrite using the correct definition of support and the flow diffeomorphism preserves every claim with no new constructions.

issues.failure_explanation: The change of variables x ↦ x + ∫_{t1}^{t2} A(s(τ),τ)dτ is the flow map of dx/dt = A(x,t), not a rigid translation. The integral ∫ A(s(τ),τ)dτ depends on the starting point x through the trajectory s(τ; x), so its derivative with respect to x is not zero. The Jacobian of the flow map is det(DΦ) = exp(∫ ∇·A dτ) by Liouville's formula, which equals 1 only when ∇·A = 0. For a general velocity field the L^P norm of ψ is not preserved. Concrete counterexample: A(x) = 2x in one dimension gives ψ(x,t1) = Ψ(cx) with c = e^{2(t2−t1)}, so ‖ψ‖_{L^P} = c^{−1/P}‖Ψ‖_{L^P} ≠ ‖Ψ‖_{L^P}. The same false step appears in Lemma lemma-psi-Omega-LP. Lemma-f-H*'s proof cites Lemma lemma-psi-Omega-LP to claim ‖V‖_{L^2(G)} = ‖W‖_{L^2(G)}, and Theorem thm-NumericalSolution-Stability's proof uses the same false equality to derive its per-element estimate. Theorem thm-NumericalSolution-Uniqueness invokes the stability proof and inherits the same invalid step.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the L^P norm equalities in both lemmas with Jacobian-weighted bounds (‖ψ(·,t1)‖_{L^P} ≤ C‖Ψ‖_{L^P} with C = exp(½∫|∇·A|dτ)) or add the hypothesis ∇·A = 0, then update Lemma Lemma-f-H*'s proof to use the corrected bound (with ‖W‖_{L^2(Φ(G))} ≤ ‖W‖_{L^2(G)} for W supported in G) and adjust the constant in Theorem thm-NumericalSolution-Stability accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The L^P norm invariance statements of Lemma lemma-psi-Rd-LP and Lemma lemma-psi-Omega-LP are false for velocity fields with ∇·A ≠ 0. Lemma Lemma-f-H*'s boundedness proof uses the false equality and additionally misapplies the norm identity to the wrong domain. Theorem thm-NumericalSolution-Stability's proof chain (per-element L^2 estimate) is invalid. Theorem thm-NumericalSolution-Uniqueness inherits the same broken step through its reference to the stability proof. Theorem thm-NumericalScheme-Existence depends on Lemma Lemma-f-H* through the Riesz argument. The conclusions of Lemma Lemma-f-H*, the existence theorem, the stability theorem, and the uniqueness theorem can all be recovered with modified arguments (Jacobian-weighted bounds), but the exact L^P norm preservation guarantee is lost for non-incompressible flows.
issues.title: L^P norm invariance of the adjoint is false for general velocity fields
issues.why_classification: The lemmas' statements change from exact equality to a Jacobian-weighted bound (or gain an added incompressibility hypothesis), but the main theorems (existence, stability, uniqueness) all survive with modified constants and local proof updates. The repair requires a contained argument tracking the flow Jacobian and no new global proof architecture. The stability constant grows but still depends only on (T, Δt, Ω, A) as advertised.
